fullPassage: The idea that our senses may be deceiving us was taken up by the French philosopher and mathematician René Descartes. (C) He realized that sometimes our senses give us a false impression — a straight stick in a glass of water appears to be bent, for example. And if we know that they can be unreliable, it would be wrong to trust them completely — everything that we experience with our senses might be false. (A) It might even be that we are asleep, and that the world we are experiencing is no more than a dream, or that God or some mischievous power is making us believe things that are not really true. If that is the case, though, we can never know anything for sure. (B) But Descartes then showed that there was one thing he could be sure of: In order to be deceived, he must exist, and exist as a thing that thinks. So, although his senses could not be trusted, he could be sure he existed as something that was capable of thinking and reasoning.

"감각이 믿을 수 없다면, 감각을 __________ 신뢰하는 것은 잘못이다." (1단어)

det.korean: it would be wrong to trust them completely
det.analysis: 본문에서 wrong to trust them completely.
det.tip: completely = 완전히

questions.passage: The idea that our senses may be deceiving us was taken up by the French philosopher and mathematician René Descartes. He realized that sometimes our senses give us a false impression — a straight stick in a glass of water appears to be bent, for example. And if we know that they can be unreliable, it would be wrong to trust them completely — everything that we experience with our senses might be false. It might even be that we are asleep, and that the world we are experiencing is no more than a dream, or that God or some mischievous power is making us believe things that are not really true. If that is the case, though, we can never know anything for sure. But Descartes then showed that there was one thing he could be sure of: In order to be deceived, he must ____, and ____ as a thing that thinks. So, although his senses could not be trusted, he could be sure he ____ed as something that was capable of thinking and reasoning.

questions.stem: 윗글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 감각에 대한 회의 → 존재 증명(사고하는 존재).
det.analysis:
❌ ① 감각의 정확성을 증명하는 과학적 실험
✅ ③ 데카르트의 감각 회의론과 존재 증명
❌ ② 프랑스 철학의 역사적 발전
❌ ④ 꿈과 현실을 구별하는 실용적 방법
✅②: 감각 회의 + 존재 증명 = 글의 핵심
❌①: 감각의 정확성 증명이 아님
❌③: 프랑스 철학 역사가 아님
❌④: 실용적 구별 방법이 아님
det.tip: 데카르트: 감각 불신 → "나는 생각한다, 고로 존재한다"

questions.stem:
윗글을 한 문장으로 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A)와 (B)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

Descartes questioned the (A) __________ of our senses but concluded that the very act of (B) __________ proves one's existence.

det.korean: 데카르트는 감각의 (A) 신뢰성(reliability)을 의심했지만, (B) 사고(thinking) 행위가 존재를 증명한다고 결론.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ (A) reliability - (B) thinking
❌ ② (A) importance - (B) sleeping
❌ ③ (A) reliability - (B) dreaming
❌ ① (A) beauty - (B) thinking
✅① (A) reliability — (B) thinking: unreliable → thinking proves existence
❌② sleeping: 잠은 결론이 아님
❌③ dreaming: 꿈은 중간 과정
❌④ beauty: 아름다움 — 무관
det.tip: reliability(신뢰성) + thinking(사고)
